events.content:
Done. All four routes' pieces are in place, using React's `<ViewTransition>` (no config flag needed — Next 16's App Router runs on a React canary that exports it).

**What changed**

`app/ProductGrid.tsx` — each thumbnail is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`} share="morph" default="none">`, and the `<Link>` carries `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`.

`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` — the hero uses the *same* `name`, so React pairs it with the thumbnail and morphs size/position. The back link carries `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`. The hero renders outside the `Suspense` boundary, so it lands in the same commit as the navigation, which is what the morph requires.

`app/PageTransition.tsx` (new) — shared wrapper mapping `nav-forward`/`nav-back` to directional enter/exit classes, with `default: 'none'` so untyped navigations (browser back/forward, `router.refresh()`, Suspense reveals) don't slide. It's used inside each `page.tsx` rather than the layout, since layouts persist and their enter/exit never fire.

`app/page.tsx` + detail page — Suspense fallbacks wrapped with `exit="slide-down"`, contents with `enter="slide-up"`, so skeleton→content is a handoff rather than a pop.

`app/globals.css` — `::view-transition-*` rules for `.morph` (400ms with a mid-flight blur to hide interpolation artifacts), `.slide-up`/`.slide-down` (fast 150ms exit, gentler delayed 210ms enter), and `.nav-forward`/`.nav-back` (±60px horizontal slide). Plus `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }` so clicks aren't swallowed mid-animation.

`react-canary.d.ts` (new) — one-line `react/canary` types reference so `ViewTransition` typechecks against the installed `@types/react`.

**Reduced motion:** a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block zeroes `animation-duration`/`animation-delay` on all `::view-transition-group/image-pair/old/new` pseudo-elements, so content swaps instantly. I also stopped the pre-existing skeleton `pulse` animation there, since you asked for all animations to respect the preference.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` succeeds, both routes serve 200 with no runtime errors (proof `ViewTransition` resolves — an undefined component would throw during SSR), and the shipped CSS chunk contains every pseudo-element rule un-mangled by the minifier. I could not confirm the animations visually — there's no browser in this sandbox — so the timing/feel is worth an eyeball in Chrome.

One behavioral note: browser-initiated back (button or swipe gesture) carries no transition type, so the directional slide deliberately won't play there; the shared-element morph still does.
